doc.title: Bobby Shew interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 1, 2020

title: Playing lead for Benny Goodman at the Tropicana
summary: Goodman moves Shew onto lead and solos ahead of Wes Hensel, stares at him from the next chair, never praises him, and Mavis Rivers sings with the band.

story.theme_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the leader and his bands
story.community_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the perfectionist bandleader

blocks.x: Oh that’s right. I remember Joe talking about Benny you know. I think the thing with Benny was I don’t really know if Benny even had a clue to himself. I really don’t know. He was such a brilliant player, I mean, what a great clarinet player, absolutely you know. But I swear when I was on the band I was on there twice. And the first time it was his band and I was hired in the section and Wes Hensel was hired as the lead player. Wes was the great lead player with Les Brown’s band for many years back in the 40s and all that stuff you know. And Wes was a great trumpet player. He was not a jazz player but he was a great arranger and everything. But we were at the first rehearsal and Benny kept staring at the trumpet section. And we’re playing you know. And he’s just staring at the trumpet section. And I’m going like what the hell is going on with this guy. And I was very young and you know, kind of like green and didn’t know what was going on. I was thrilled to be with Benny Goodman but you know, and the band was like it was an all-star band, Georgie Auld was on the band, and Lou Levy was the piano player. Colin Bailey on drums, Monty Budwig on bass. Are you kidding me? And I mean Carl Fontana was on the band, Jimmy Gwynn I mean come on give me a break. I mean look who’s in this band you know? And, but he kept staring at the trumpet section. After a while he called a break. And this guy, I think his name was Larry Grayson, he was kind of Benny’s manager. He came over and we were kind of just standing around and he came over to me and he said, “Bobby I need to talk to you.” And I went oh boy, here I go, I said, “Look, Larry, I mean it must be something about me he doesn’t like. But it’s okay, I’m just going, you don’t have to patronize me I’m out of here.” He says, “Oh no, no, no, no, Benny wants you on lead.” So I went, “What?” He said, “He wants you on lead, he doesn’t like the way Wes is playing lead.” He moved Wes Hensel to fourth chair, put me on all the lead, Jack Sheldon was sitting next to me in the trumpet section, and Carl Saunders was in the section. And I had to play all the lead and all of the solos. He wouldn’t let Jack Sheldon play any solos. I had to memorize all of the Harry James’ things on all of those pieces, and go out front, memorized, and play them. And it was like unbelievable. And I thought damn. Right? You mean like now? Right now? And then here’s the other funny thing was Jack was like the comedian. He would go out front and do a little ten minutes of comedy. And when he did that Benny would come back in the session and sit in Jack’s chair. And Jack had some charts so we’d play, back him up while he sang you know? And Benny would sit right to my left and turn like this and stare at me. Like his face is twelve inches away from my face and I’m trying to play and © Fillius Jazz Archive -6-
Benny’s sitting there looking at me like, staring at me. I’m going holy crap, you want to talk about a heartbeat. My pulse was about 500.
Oh well I’m sure he gave you a big raise for all that double duty.

No. Nothing. And he never said one complimentary word to me, not once ever. Not once ever. And it was just, we did four weeks at the Tropicana Hotel with that band. And it was — we had, who else did we have on there, oh we had Mavis Rivers is the singer. Remember her?
Oh yes she was a great singer. She’s from Samoa. Yeah. You know Matt Catingub the saxophone player?
